sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Franchise Licensing and Syrups Supply Chain for Bubble Tea Chains

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Federal Common Law; Quebec Private Law under Civil Law tradition)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada–China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA) 2014

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17; Criminal Code RSC 1985 c C-46; Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1; An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Canadian Sanctions Regulations, SOR/2019-51; Special Economic Measures Act, RSC 1985 c S-8

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of name reservation certificate issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
Certified corporate extract and Certificate of Good Standing of the ultimate beneficial owner's parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (if jurisdiction is not a member of the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of identity and address for each director, officer, and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary / Commissioner for Oaths in country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against FINTRAC guidance, Canadian sanctions under SEMA, UN Security Council consolidated lists, OFAC SDN list, and domestic PEP lists. Enhanced due diligence required for politically exposed persons, foreign PEPs, heads of international organizations, and their close associates. Screening thresholds follow FINTRAC's beneficial ownership requirement of 25% or more, with reputational risk assessment elevated for cross-border franchise and royalty arrangements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Services en ligne / Nom d'entreprise (REQ online name search and reservation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Quebec Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) requires the primary business name to be in French unless exempt under regulation. Latin transliteration is mandatory for non-French proper names. The name must comply with the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business, and be distinct, non-misleading, and not contrary to public order.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative review request with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec within 30 days of the refusal, citing reasons and providing supporting evidence. If the administrative review confirms refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Court of Québec (Chambre civile) or the Superior Court of Québec for judicial review within the applicable statutory limitaion period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be accepted for the registered office address only if it provides a physical street address in Quebec and legal service-of-process arrangements. However for a franchisor operating under ISIC 5610 and maintaining a supply chain, commercial substance requirements mandate a physical operational presence in Quebec, including administrative office, inventory management location, and franchise support staff.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to Moderate (approx. 15% within first 18 months if fully compliant with Quebec enterprise legal publicity, tax, and food safety regulations; higher if the business is selected for FINTRAC or Revenu Québec audit).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and reservation fee (Quebec business name)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises

Notarization of UBO identity and address documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff in jurisdiction of notarization

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille for Quebec name reservation certificate and UBO parent documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Global Affairs Canada (Authentication and Service of Documents Section)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee per apostille ($25 CAD per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO, PEP, and sanctions screening service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory government fee and additional legal processing

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c S-31.1, ss. 5 (incorporation), 8 (articles), 15 (existence), 16 (certificate), 105-109 (directors and officers), and 214-216 (corporate records); implemented together with the Act respecting the legal publicity of sole proprietorships, partnerships and legal persons (CQLR c P-45).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (QUE) — Registraire des entreprises; electronic filing portal CLIC at https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution) filed electronically through the Registraire's CLIC system, including the automatic registration (immatriculation) of the legal person in the Quebec enterprise register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow-account requirement under the QBCA. The Articles must authorize at least one class of shares; the board may lawfully fix a nominal consideration (e.g., CAD 1 per common share) or approve payment in property. For banking and franchise operations a commercial opening capital of CAD 1,000–10,000 is recommended.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, as accepted on this date, are hereby adopted and ratified; that the subscribers listed in Schedule A subscribe for and receive the number and class of shares indicated opposite their names, for such consideration as the board has approved; that the registered office of the corporation shall be fixed at the address stated in the Articles, in Quebec, effective immediately; that [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Treasurer, and [Name] Secretary, each to hold office at pleasure for the ensuing fiscal year; and that the directors and officers are authorized, jointly or separately, to execute and file all registration, bank, and licensing documents required to give full effect to these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name due diligence and optional name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — CLIC online portal / Registre des entreprises check page.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify availability and compliance of the proposed corporate designation (French primacy rules under the Charter of the French Language). Submit an optional Name Reservation Request (Demande de réservation de nom) online to secure the designation for 90 days. The Registraire performs an automatic conflict check against existing names and trademarks in the Quebec register.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (French and English versions)
Power of attorney if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or contested, file a written objection or request a new name; alternatively submit a revised designated name and pay an additional processing fee. The Registraire may also require a renunciation or consent-letter from a prior rights holder within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and payment of statutory fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — CLIC electronic filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the standardized Articles of Incorporation form via CLIC. Insert the authorized capital, class conditions and any restrictions on transfer. Provide the proposed registered office address (Quebec physical address). Pay the CAD 300 filing fee online by credit card or Interac. The registraire will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and the NEQ number upon approval.
required_dossiers: Completed Articles of Incorporation form (CLIC data entry)
Initial director information (name, address, residency status)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, obtain the Registraire's refusal reason letter, correct the deficiencies (e.g., invalid share clause or non-compliant name), and re-file through the same CLIC transaction within the prescribed period. Fast-track correction is available where only minor information was omitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and enterprise register activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec — Corporate registry service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Validate the electronic Certificate of Incorporation (Certificat de constitution) and the assigned Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). The NEQ serves as the master identifier for provincial tax, employer and licensing registrations. Confirm that the enterprise registration is publicly posted in the register as of the certificate date.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NEQ notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any data in the certificate is inaccurate, file a 'Demande de correction' with the Registraire within 30 days of issuance; the corrected certificate will be reissued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting and organizational resolutions (share subscription, officers, by-laws)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the corporation — corporate statutory records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of directors or adopt a unanimous written consent. Adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution in the incorporation legal framework; approve share allotment and issuance to subscribers; elect the President, Treasurer and Secretary; adopt the general operating by-law (By-law No. 1). Records must be placed in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Share certificates and register of allotments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any organizational act is later found deficient (e.g., omitted officer election), ratify it by means of a written consent resolution signed by all directors and, where required, all shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Declare and perfect the registered office and prepare statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec / corporate statutory records at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is the physical address declared in the articles (a post-office box is not sufficient). Keep the Register of Directors, Register of Shareholders, and any transfer ledger in the minute book, updated with the name and address of each director and shareholder. Any change of registered office must be filed as a Declaration of Modification with the Registraire within 30 days.
required_dossiers: Physical address of registered office (lease or authorization)
List of directors and officers with residential addresses
Register of shareholders and share allotment record
Minute book with by-laws and consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing of a change of registered office triggers penalties under the Legal Publicity Act; apply promptly to the Registraire and, if sanctioned, request cancellation of the sanction under the administrative review procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal incorporation and tax registrations: CRA Business Number, GST/HST and payroll accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register on BRO using the federal jurisdiction code and corporation details. Obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) and open a GST/HST account for taxable supplies (boba tea beverages, franchise royalty fees). Open a payroll trust account if the company will employ staff. The BN Program account structure will include corporate income tax automatically.
required_dossiers: Legal name and mailing address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the GST/HST registration is denied or delayed, contact the CRA business window for a manual review; the BN account can generally be backdated 30 days from the date of the application. Voluntary disclosure is available for unintentional failures to register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Quebec provincial registrations: Revenu Québec QST/TVQ employer and consumption tax accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec — Entreprises services en ligne (e-services).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for the Quebec Sales Tax (TVQ / QST) using the NEQ as the key identifier. Register as an employer for the Quebec Parental Insurance Plan (RQAP), the health services contribution, and any other mandatory payroll deductions under the Act respecting the Régie de l'assurance maladie du Québec. Set up remittance frequency based on expected taxable turnover.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the QST registration is filed late, Revenu Québec will still backdate the account to the date of first taxable activity; file a REQ-215? For penalties, request remission or penalty relief based on reasonable cause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open corporate bank account and complete subscription capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canadian chartered bank (e.g., major Schedule I bank) — corporate account opening officer.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the corporate package to a commercial banking centre. Execute the bank account resolution separately, or rely on the board resolution authorizing officers to open bank accounts. Wire the subscription capital amounts (as resolved) into the corporate operating account. Keep the deposit slip in the accounting records. No statutory minimum capital applies, but the bank may require an opening deposit of at least CAD 1,000.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation
Directors resolution / officer authorization for bank signing
Directors' identification documents (two forms per Canadian AML rules)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional beneficial-ownership or source-of-funds documentation, provide a corporate register extract and share certificates evidencing the same; request a written waiver of any excessive onboarding conditions after the corporate identity package has been validated.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ) — Direction générale de la transformation alimentaire, for the food processing establishment permit; Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) for Safe Food for Canadians Act licensing of interprovincial/export trade.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Processing Establishment Permit (Permis de transformation alimentaire) issued by MAPAQ; if the franchise distributes syrups, concentrates or finished boba products across provincial or international borders, a Safe Food for Canadians Act Licence is additionally required from the CFIA.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) — Direction générale de l'évaluation environnementale, under the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c Q-2).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II — Declaration of Compliance (Déclaration de conformité) / Screening Registration; a full EIA study is not required for a small to medium beverage manufacturing and warehousing facility generating effluent below 5,000 L/day and volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions below 15,000 kg/year.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: BOD5 ≤ 500 mg/L, TSS ≤ 600 mg/L, pH 5.5–10.0, oil and grease ≤ 100 mg/L, in accordance with municipal sewer by-laws and provincial criteria; atmospheric emissions: CO and NOx thresholds for fuel-burning equipment under the Règlement sur l'assainissement de l'atmosphère; waste handling: pearl tapioca waste and syrup solids must be stored in sealed containers and disposed of at a permitted facility, with no unauthorized discharge to municipal stormwater systems.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety: obtain a fire safety permit from the local municipal fire service (Service de sécurité incendie), verify occupancy classification and emergency egress standards; Structural Load Inspection: engineering sign-off on mezzanine storage racks, heavy syrup pallet loads, and HVAC equipment anchoring; Occupational Clearance: register as an employer with CNESST (Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail), complete a workplace risk assessment, affix the 'Avis de conformité' and retain a CNESST prevention program file in the workplace.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA-ARC) — Business Registration Online (BRO/IE) and My Business Account; concurrent Quebec registration with Revenu Québec / Registraire d'entreprises du Québec (REQ) via the CLIC 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' portal for QST, QPIP, CNESST, and provincial payroll accounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign franchisor establishing a Quebec Business Corporation must: (1) obtain a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) by F.1 submit to CRA via Business Registration Online (www.canada.ca/business-registration) or Form RC1; (2) request a GST/HST 'RT' program account automatically with the BN; (3) file Quebec incorporation/registration with REQ (Form AR-1) and open a Revenu Québec file to obtain a QST account 'Telechargeur' ID; (4) appoint a Canadian resident representative (agent for service) if no place of business in Canada; (5) register for payroll, RDTP, QPIP, and CSST accounts if domestic employees exist; (6) obtain the unique 'NEQ' (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec) as the single provincial business identifier aligned with the BN. Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada must also register under ETA section 240(1) even below the small-supplier threshold in certain cases (e.g., soliciting orders or maintaining an establishment).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Canada/Quebec Business Corporation is a separate taxpayer under ITA Part I (Federal 15% general rate) and Quebec Tax Act Part I (11.5% base rate after general reduction), with permanent-establishment apportionment in Quebec. Canada taxes worldwide income of resident corporations on a territorial-plus basis with foreign tax credits; no check-the-box pass-through regime exists for corporations. Quebec is not a designated tax-exempt zone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no federal check-the-box election. Available entity-level statutory elections include: (1) subsection 85(1) and 85(2) rollover elections on incorporation/transfer of property; (2) section 256/256.1 amalgamation election and 88(1) wind-up rollover; (3) subsection 216(1) election by non-residents to compute Canadian rental income tax on a net basis; (4) Part XIV (non-resident Part XII.6) 25% branch tax election; (5) foreign affiliate 'surplus' elections (S.90, 113, 128-131) and FAPI grouping under 91(4); (6) hybrid mismatch structural elections — Canada's EIFEL regime (section 18.2/18.3) denies excessive interest and financing expense where group entities treat the same arrangement inconsistently (dual inclusion/omission), with election to align timing under 18.2(6) for specified entities; (7) GST/HST section 156 election for closely related corporations to treat limited supplies as non-taxable; (8) QST/GST combined filing consistency election and B2B 'net tax' election; (9) section 159 election to reduce withholding tax on a Canadian corporation paying management fees to non-residents.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Excise Tax Act, Part IX) in Quebec + Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ, Tax Administration Act); a dual VAT credit-invoice system in which Quebec administers the GST as a partner jurisdiction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 worldwide taxable supplies (GST/HST small-supplier threshold under ETA s.148(1)); CAD 30,000 taxable supplies in Canada for QST (TAA s. 375); once exceeded, mandatory registration, with effect from the calendar quarter in which the threshold is exceeded or, for a new supplier, the day the first supply is made. For franchise royalties cross-border: non-resident franchisors licensing to Quebec franchisees must register for GST/HST and QST even below the threshold where they solicit orders, maintain an establishment, or derive Canadian-source royalties (agency/permanent-establishment rules), and must collect QST on royalty installments unless the supply is zero-rated (export) or subject to self-assessment by the Quebec registrant under the reverse-charge for services (TAA s. 87.1).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API tax stamping, or 'valeur fiscale' digital stamping regime exists in Canada. Instead: (1) mandatory electronic filing of GST/HST net-file or Revenu Québec ITGS for registrants filing monthly or above the threshold; (2) pan-Canadian e-invoicing is voluntary under the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 framework (Canada's 'E-invoicing' service, launched by the governments of Quebec and Ontario in 2023) but not a legal mandate; (3) invoice content must satisfy ETA s. 223 and Quebec TAA s. 435 minimum data (supplier name, BN, date, description, GST/QST payable or included, rate); (4) POS terminals in boba outlets must issue receipts showing the GST and QST components; (5) simplified (point-of-sale) QST/GST invoice rules permit combined display only if both taxes are shown when the transaction is taxable; (6) in Quebec, a registrant must issue an invoice within 30 days if requested and preserve records for 6 years (CRA) / 7 years (Revenu Québec).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated under ETA Sch. VI, Part V (s.1) where the supplier ships or delivers the goods to a non-resident customer outside Canada and the goods are exported 'as soon as practicable' (in practice within 60 days) by the supplier or at the direction of the supplier via a common carrier for export; processed tea/syrup and franchise boba equipment shipped to US or foreign franchisees qualify if the exporter obtains evidence of export (customs declaration, bills of lading) before the return is filed. Services: zero-rated under ETA Sch. VI, Part V (s.7) where the supply is made to a non-resident and the service is not performed in Canada; franchise licensing, royalties, training, marketing support, and supply-chain coordination services supplied to foreign franchisees are zero-rated if the royalty or service is 'in respect of' a business carried on by the non-resident outside Canada and no Canadian situs of performance exists; if part is performed in Canada (e.g., R&D or Canadian franchisee services), apportionment is required. Royalties from foreign franchisees are not subject to QST where the franchise agreement is a genuine export supply, and Revenu Québec applies a similar non-resident + no use in Quebec test. Digital supply of software or cloud-based franchise management systems follows OECD/ETA e-commerce rules: zero-rated when delivered to the foreign franchisee's business address outside Canada and not used by a Quebec establishment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency B13A / Canada Customs Invoice / GCA Export Declaration or certified carrier exit confirmation; for US-bound goods, the ACE/AES filing accepted as export evidence)
Commercial Invoice and Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (showing foreign consignee, Incoterms EXW/FOB, description, quantity, invoice value, country of origin CAN, EORI or US importer number)

Inward Remittance Certificate or signed proof of FX receipt from the non-resident franchisee (bank SWIFT/MT103, wire confirmation denominated in CAD or foreign currency showing funds credited to the Canadian exporter's account)

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC) acts as the monetary and exchange-rate authority; exchange controls are not administered by the Bank. Foreign-exchange and cross-border transfer monitoring is conducted by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) and prudential oversight of banks by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). The Canadian dollar is legal tender under the Currency Act, and there is no central foreign-exchange licensing body.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. Canada operates an open capital account with no quantitative restrictions on foreign direct investment, profit repatriation, dividends, royalties, or loan repayments. Quebec imposes no provincial capital controls; funds may be remitted freely through chartered banks. Non-resident shareholders face no withholding tax beyond the standard Part XIII rates under the Canada–Quebec tax framework, subject to treaty relief. Profit remittance is accomplished via ordinary wire transfers with proper tax forms (NR4/income declaration) and no prior approval from the Bank of Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds exists under Canadian federal or Quebec law. Exporters may maintain foreign-currency accounts in Canadian Schedule I banks and repatriate earnings at market rates. FINTRAC only requires reporting of cross-border wire transfers exceeding CAD 10,000. The boba tea franchise's syrups and equipment export revenue may be held in USD or CAD without conversion timetable.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low direct viability. Foreign electronic money institutions (EMIs) and offshore digital banks are not permitted to carry on the business of banking in Canada unless licensed or chartered under the Bank Act or operating as an authorized foreign bank branch with OSFI approval. Offshore EMIs may offer payment-processing or prepaid-card rails to the Canadian entity only via partnerships with federally regulated Canadian financial institutions or money-services businesses registered with FINTRAC. AML/CFT obligations require EMI transactions to flow through a Canadian clearing partner to access Payments Canada rails. For this low-risk franchise structure, an EMI can serve as a supplemental collection node but not as the primary liquidity account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted for a Canadian-incorporated business with Canadian resident directors. FINTRAC-compliant identity verification can be performed by reliable methods including video conferencing, digital identity services, or notarized copies of identification. However, if all directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) are non-residents, most Tier 1 Canadian banks require at least one director to attend an in-branch interview in Canada or provide a notarized, apostilled KYC package plus a solicitor's certificate. Quebec-headquartered banks may impose enhanced due diligence for franchise entities where brand royalties pass through cross-border chains. A physical presence visit is not statutorily mandatory for low-risk entities, but the bank's own risk-based policies may mandate it for material non-resident UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO(s) holding more than 25% of shares and inability to identify source of funds for franchise capital escrow injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate register extract from Registraire des entreprises (Quebec), certified certificate of incorporation, UBO declaration form, sworn source-of-wealth statement, audited financial statements of the franchise parent entity, bank reference letters from the home-country institution, and notarized board resolution listing the direct capital injection as a franchise expansion investment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction payment for Global Franchise rights fee or syrup supply pre-payment from an OFAC-sanctioned or FATF-monitored corridor
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original franchise agreement, licensing royalty schedules, commercial invoices from the supply contract, third-party customs declarations, transport bills of lading, and a FinCEN/FINTRAC-compliant beneficial ownership certification demonstrating no sanctioned-party nexus. Where the counterparty location is non-sanctioned but high jurisdictional risk, include a transaction-specific legal opinion from a Canadian counsel and sanctions screening results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large cash-equivalent POS deposits from boba tea retail locations without supporting sales records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Daily sales logs, transactional POS reconciliation reports, franchisee audit confirmations, provincial sales tax (QST) filings, and an independent CPA review of cash-flow patterns. A voluntary anti-money-laundering compliance program and concurrent internal audit report should be submitted to the bank's financial crimes unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Syrup import prepayment routing through an unrelated third-party intermediary within a 48-hour rapid turnaround, suggesting trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full trade finance package including signed purchase orders, inspection certificates, shipping documents, container tracking, LC or SWIFT MT103 records, and intercompany pre-payment justification. A legal cover memo explaining the supply-chain rationale for intermediary routing and confirmation that the intermediary is not a shell entity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol for the initial franchise capital escrow from non-resident parent or shareholders: settle via SWIFT MT103 into the Canadian entity's capital escrow account at a Tier 1 Canadian bank. Use Fedwire/CHIPS or SWIFT single-customer-credit-transfer formatting; include a purpose-of-payment code corresponding to 'Foreign Direct Investment in enterprise capital' to satisfy the reporting thresholds under Canada's Balance of Payments reporting to Statistics Canada via the Bank of Canada's International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS) if above CAD 50,000. Provide a board resolution authorizing the inward transfer, a UBO declaration, and a simple narrative reference 'Franchise capital contribution for ISIC 5610 operation' to reduce bank holds. For sums above CAD 10,000, the bank files an Electronic Funds Transfer Report with FINTRAC. No exchange-control approval is required. Funds may be held immediately in CAD or USD sub-ledgers and swapped into CAD using a spot trade.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for franchise royalties, syrup inventory imports, and equipment purchases shall use SWIFT MT103 single payment instructions for interbank wire settlements; a commercial letter of credit (LC) via SWIFT MT700 issued by the Canadian bank is required for high-value recurring edible-syrup containers and specialized tea-making machines. The preferred clearing rails are: (1) Payments Canada Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for CAD-denominated high-value payments between Canadian bank accounts; (2) SWIFT gpi covered MT103 for international corporate wire; (3) UCP600-compliant documentary LC with MT710/MT720 negotiation for cross-border trade flows. Settlement currencies may be CAD or USD; if the foreign beneficiary requires payment in CNY/TWD/USD, a corresponding currency account in the payor bank's nostro ledger or a spot FX transaction is used. All outbound transfers above CAD 10,000 trigger FINTRAC reporting. Royalty disbursements to the global franchise parent must include a tax memo for Quebec Part XIII withholding and a valid NR4 filing where applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards with a licensed Canadian Schedule I bank or an OSFI-authorized counterparty

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing exotic currencies (e.g., CNY, TWD, VND) where the franchise supply-chain payments originate, provided the Canadian entity is a permitted eligible contract participant
Cross-currency swaps between CAD and USD for capital-structure management and recurring royal payments
Plain vanilla FX options (call/put) on CAD/USD for downside protection on imported-syrup costs
Outright spot and swap transactions under the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement with a Canadian bank

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal CBCA Annual Return for non-distributing corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No fee for online filing; paper filing costs CAD 40 (approx. US$30). Failure to file for two consecutive years permits the Director to initiate administrative dissolution under CBCA s. 212; a dissolved corporation must be revived by court order or reinstatement before carrying on business.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 15% + Quebec 11.5% = 26.5% combined general corporate income tax rate for a Quebec permanent establishment
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction: federal 9% plus Quebec 4.5%, combined approximately 13.5% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income. No general corporate tax holiday is available. Preferential deductions include the SR&ED expenditure pool, Quebec patent-box/IP deduction, and manufacturing/processing rate reductions where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed via CRA T2 E-file / TELEFILE or CRA My Business Account for the Canada Revenue Agency.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is the last day of the sixth month after fiscal year-end; balance due date is two months after fiscal year-end, or three months for a CCPC eligible for the small business deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name as registered under the Canada Business Corporations Act and the Quebec corporate register.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the registered non-resident corporate name; the name must correspond with the treaty residence certificate if treaty relief is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CRA business number and RP/RZ program account identification for corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada must obtain a CRA business number and file a T2 using the Canadian permanent establishment profile.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter NAICS 722515 and describe the franchising of bubble tea stores, franchise licensing, and the supply of syrups and tea ingredients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Clearly state Canadian-source business activities; a mere agency or buying office is insufficient to support a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Worldwide taxable income computed under the Income Tax Act after loss carryovers and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate Canadian-source business income under provincial income tax regulations based on the Quebec permanent establishment's gross revenue and salary ratios.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim the federal small business deduction on active business income up to CAD 500,000, subject to aggregate investment limits and taxable capital.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned corporation generally cannot claim the small business deduction for income derived from Canadian permanent establishment operations unless it qualifies as a CCPC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Part I tax after general rate reduction, federal credits, and the Quebec abatement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident, compute Part I tax only on the Canadian permanent establishment's taxable income and enter treaty, if applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 5% of the unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months. Repeated failure to file may attract 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months. Gross negligence penalties are 50% of the understatement. Unpaid balances bear compounded daily prescribed rate interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec CO-17.T Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically through Revenu Québec's Mon dossier d'entreprise or approved E-file software.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is the last day of the sixth month after fiscal year-end; provincial balance due date is generally two months after year-end, with instalment rules applying to larger corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise number assigned by the Registraire des entreprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with a Quebec establishment must obtain an NEQ and identify the local representative or agent, if any.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the exact date of the fiscal year end; must align with the federal T2 period unless a special Quebec election applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Quebec fiscal period for a non-resident must match the period used for the federal T2 permanent establishment allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter NAICS 722515 and the Quebec economic activity description for bubble tea franchise operations and syrup supply chain.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No special non-resident instruction beyond accurate classification of the Quebec business activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income after federal adjustments, provincial loss carryovers, and scientific research and innovation deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents use income earned from carrying on business through a Quebec establishment; the amount must be consistent with the federal T2 PE allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the Quebec general rate of 11.5% or the reduced 4.5% small-business rate where eligible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations are subject to the general rate on Quebec PE income; no Quebec small-business deduction is available unless a special resident status applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim Quebec film, e-business, patent-box, and other refundable/non-refundable credits for which the corporation is eligible.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treaty and Quebec tax credit claims require proof that the economic activity is performed in Quebec by employees and premises of the permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Québec imposes a late-filing penalty of 5% of the balance owed plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; interest is compounded daily at the provincial prescribed rate. A false or misleading return may trigger a 50% gross-negligence penalty.
